# Neglected tropical diseases

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Infectious diseases > Other infectious diseases > Neglected tropical diseases*

## Summary

Neglected tropical diseases are a diverse group of medical conditions (see Overview below) found mainly in tropical regions that disproportionately affect impoverished communities, women, and children with often severe health, economic, and social consequences. As a disease class, <u>NTDs</u> affect more than one billion people worldwide. Controlling these diseases is difficult not only because of their neglect arising from the low <u>socioeconomic status</u> of the people they predominantly affect, but also because of the fact that they are mostly <u>vector</u>-borne and include various parasitic infections that involve complex life cycles and domestic animal reservoirs. <u>Buruli ulcer</u> and <u>mycetoma</u> are treated here; the other <u>NTDs</u> are discussed in separate articles. <u>Buruli ulcer</u> is a chronic, necrotizing <u>skin infection</u> caused by <u>Mycobacterium ulcerans</u>. It typically begins as a painless <u>nodule</u> that slowly ulcerates with undermined edges. Patients may develop <u>osteomyelitis</u>, <u>osteitis</u>, and <u>joint</u> deformities if not treated with <u>antibiotics</u> and <u>debridement</u>. <u>Mycetoma</u> is a chronic fungal (<u>eumycetoma</u>) or bacterial (<u>actinomycetoma</u>) <u>skin and soft tissue infection</u> that typically affects the lower extremities. Clinical findings include a painless ‎subcutaneous mass with multiple sinuses and seropurulent discharge ‎containing granules filled with the causative agent. Depending on the causative <u>pathogen</u>, treatment involves <u>antibiotics</u> or <u>antifungals</u>.
